messages:
Priya (Sales AE): Hey team — prepping on-prem POC with HelixCorp. They want a private, air-gapped POC using a Dedicated pool. Need a concise preflight for node readiness, service accounts, network egress, KMS, and how we hand them ephemeral API access. POC kicks off next Tue.
Rafael (Infra Eng): Got it. Key checks: GPU drivers, CUDA, container runtime, k8s version, nvidia device plugin, node labels/taints, kubelet config, kernel modules/time sync. I'll post a short checklist.
Rafael (Infra Eng): Checklist:
1) Verify GPU + driver
```bash
nvidia-smi -L
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
```
2) CUDA toolkit
```bash
nvcc --version || cat /usr/local/cuda/version.txt
```
3) Kernel and modules
```bash
lsmod | grep nvidia
dmesg | grep -i nvrm
```
4) K8s kubelet and CRI
```bash
kubectl get nodes -o wide
crictl ps || docker ps
```
Rafael (Infra Eng): 5) NVIDIA device plugin + DCGM as daemonset
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system get ds | grep nvidia
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l name=nvidia-device-plugin
```
Sam (Solutions Engineer): For private runs we also need:
- Service account for the POC with a short-lived token (we do not ship long-lived keys into air-gapped sites)
- A network route to the k8s API control plane + nodeport for health probes
- Internal DNS entries for model artifact hosts (if they don't want outbound resolution)
Nadia (FieldTech): On KMS: customer will use Vault HSM. We need a reachable endpoint for transit operations and a service account that can call KMS. Note: support is for encrypt/decrypt transit only — no external internet required if Vault is local.
Priya (Sales AE): They asked about hosted API keys — can we provide ephemeral tokens they can fetch from a bastion?
Rafael (Infra Eng): Yes. Flow we support: 
1) Admin generates a scoped POC token in Console (limited scopes) -> exports a signed blob.
2) On-prem agent or bastion POSTs the signed blob to our validate endpoint over mTLS.
3) Platform returns ephemeral session creds (1–6h) scoped to the POC.
Sam (Solutions Engineer): Important ports to document for InfoSec:
- kube-apiserver: 6443
- etcd (if self-hosted): 2379/2380
- node exporter / metrics: 9100
- NVIDIA DCGM: ~9400
- Outbound to our artifact proxy (optional): 443
Priya (Sales AE): Any driver/kernel combos we should explicitly list as unsupported?
Rafael (Infra Eng): Older R750xd kernels (<5.4) will need patches for CUDA 11.8+. We'll include a short compatibility matrix link in the checklist.
deploy-bot: Deployment plan created: poc/helixcorp/1859991234 by Sam
Nadia (FieldTech): I'll run the checklist on the first two nodes and share the outputs. Can we give them safe kubectl snippets that don't require cluster-admin?
Sam (Solutions Engineer): Use this minimal probe snippet (no cluster-admin needed):
```bash
kubectl --context=onprem get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}\n{end}'
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | egrep 'nvidia|dcgm'
```
Priya (Sales AE): Great — can we bundle everything into a one-page PDF for Legal & InfoSec and include the Dedicated pool pricing for 8x A100 pro-rated for a 30-day POC?
Sam (Solutions Engineer): Ballpark pricing: ~$XXk pro-rated for 30d for 8x A100. I'll pull exact from finance and DM you.
Rafael (Infra Eng): FYI — if they run SELinux in Enforcing mode, we recommend setting it to Permissive for the device-plugin install. Also call out cgroup v2 caveats: older runtimes like docker-19 prefer cgroup v1.
Priya (Sales AE): Thanks. I'll tag HelixCorp-ops and ask them to run the first checks tomorrow. :thumbsup:
HelixCorp-ops: We can stand up two nodes for testing. We'll run the checklist tomorrow at 10:00 PST and post results.
Priya (Sales AE): Perfect — Rafael can you review their outputs by 12:00 PST?
Rafael (Infra Eng): Yep, I'll review and call out any blockers.
Priya (Sales AE): Thanks everyone — I'll convert this into the PDF checklist and attach the pricing when finance confirms. Closing loop here.
